A1.justification: Both PDFs describe LinEAS, despite the changed title and presentation. Their complete main texts, equations, tables, figures and appendices are readable and support reliable matching across the substantial reorganization.

before.justification: V1 reports original toxicity-mitigation, sparsity, concept-composition, TruthfulQA and text-to-image experiments, including appendix results.

after.justification: V3 retains original experiments and adds human preference studies, expanded comparisons, image-steering analyses and analysis of intervention similarity against human judgments.

M1.justification: V3 Section 4.4 introduces inverse-map inference, applying the inverse learned affine transformations to induce concepts after training for removal. The core coordinate-wise affine maps, jointly optimized Wasserstein loss, sparsity penalties and optimization framework remain unchanged.

E1.justification: The image evaluation changes from COCO-based style induction and a smaller generated concept set to removal and induction across 15 concepts spanning styles, objects and perspectives. Appendix L adds 50 MEN concepts and 20 human-rated similarity pairs. Toxicity, language concept composition and TruthfulQA coverage remain; DeepSeek results are retained in the appendix.

E2.justification: V3 adds prompting, CAA with all-layer and middle-layer variants, ReFT and LoFIT-RL to toxicity comparisons, retaining LRTC-RL in Appendix E. It also adds ITI-c to image comparisons and prompting to language concept composition. These are evaluated comparators, rather than citation additions or baseline renamings.

E3.justification: Image IMGScore switches from CLIP to DINOv2-small embeddings. The revised image setup reports learning rate 1e-4 and gamma 0, versus 5e-4 and 1e-4 in v1. New protocols include a fixed-hyperparameter data sweep from 1 to 1024 examples, a language preference study with 20 volunteers and 20 prompts each, and an image study with 10 participants and 100 comparisons each. These changes preclude direct comparison of image scores across versions.

E4.justification: V3 adds a detailed data-size sensitivity sweep, DMD2 intervention-layer and sparsity sweeps, and analysis relating intervention similarity to human semantic judgments. Appendix K expands layer-support analysis into separate bias and weight panels. Earlier toxicity sparsity, composition and TruthfulQA analyses remain, often relocated.

E5.justification: Appendix L adds statistical correlation estimation between intervention similarities and human judgments over 20 MEN pairs. Existing repeat counts remain four generation seeds for toxicity, three sparsity sweeps and five seeds for TruthfulQA. The PDFs do not establish increased repetitions for retained experiments or new significance-testing procedures.

E6.justification: V3 adds substantial baseline, ablation and human-evaluation results, including LinEAS preference shares of 57.70% for language and 63.3% for images. Table 1 changes the reported Qwen-7B LinEAS RTP/TET toxicity values from 1.88/15.39 to 1.95/14.95, although v3 Table 9 retains the earlier values. TruthfulQA results remain numerically unchanged; the replacement image results use different tasks and metrics.

T1.justification: V3 Equation D.1 corrects the L2 proximal threshold from lambda1 in v1 Equation 7 to tau. Algorithm 1 removes an extra affine transformation of activations already transformed in their definition. Appendix B.1 adds computational and memory complexity expressions. The central loss and regularization mathematics remain, without a new theorem or proof framework.

C1.justification: The central contribution remains joint distributional learning of sparse affine interventions. V3 expands the headline image claim to concept mitigation and induction, narrows the advertised support reduction from 100–1000 times to 100 times, and deemphasizes compositionality as a headline contribution while retaining its results.

C2.justification: V3 adds substantive qualifications about evaluating paired-data methods on unpaired toxicity data and applying interventions indiscriminately to all tokens. It contextualizes composition success against prompting at 19% versus 17%, and distinguishes the contribution of end-to-end training from sparsity. New interpretations address UNet sparsity sensitivity and inverse-map behavior; Appendix A replaces the generic impact statement with discussion of harmful conditioning and safeguards.

D1.justification: V3 adds GPU specifications, memory requirements, timing tables across language models and DMD2, and implementation settings for the added baselines. It supplies exact prompting baselines and expanded image-prompt examples. The first page provides a code-repository link where v1 only promised release; the PDFs do not verify repository availability. Existing PPO hyperparameters and TruthfulQA procedures are retained.

R1.justification: Related work is reorganized from single-property versus multi-property steering into strong versus weak supervision, substantially changing LinEAS's positioning around unpaired data and oracle access. V3 adds discussion of BitFit, LoRA and diffusion-guidance approaches, while removing the dedicated multi-property discussion and its associated works, including van der Weij, Liu, Scalena and Zhang.

P1.justification: V3 retitles the paper and substantially rewrites the abstract, introduction, related work and image-evaluation narrative. Optimization details, refitting, composition and group-sparsity discussion move into appendices, while data sensitivity and a dedicated limitations section enter the main text. This is extensive narrative restructuring beyond adding experiments.

P2.justification: V3 replaces the two-column main layout with a single-column report and redesigns the opening illustration. It expands comparison tables, adds preference and timing tables, data-sensitivity plots and correlation heatmaps, and replaces the image galleries with induction/removal displays. The formerly combined composition/support figure is separated, with support distributions expanded into four panels.

improvement.justification: V3 substantially strengthens v1's reliance on a narrow comparator set and automated quality measures through additional evaluated baselines, human preference studies in both modalities, and targeted data-size and image-steering robustness analyses. Clearer supervision caveats, limitations, mathematical corrections and implementation disclosures make the claims easier to assess. These benefits outweigh remaining reporting problems, notably inconsistent Qwen values between Tables 1 and 9 and reversed CLIPScore direction arrows in Table 15. The improvement concerns evidential quality, not a demonstrated same-setting performance increase.
